scope: Primary-source bibliography and interpretation for a 28-day budget-constrained evaluation study; proposed experiments have not been run.
citation_convention: BibTeX uses first arXiv submission year unless a journal or conference record is explicitly cited. Latest checked revisions may be later. Differences below are proposed positioning, not proven novelty claims.

sources.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
sources.verified_material: Metadata and abstract on arXiv; official ICLR 2025 paper record.
sources.original_contribution: Defines Automated Design of Agentic Systems and demonstrates Meta Agent Search: a meta agent writes agent code using an archive of prior designs, with experiments spanning multiple tasks and transfer settings.
sources.our_difference: RSI-Audit keeps a small open-model backbone and mutation space fixed, and studies how validation-budget allocation changes final independent audit performance. It does not claim to invent automated agent design or archive search.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: The original automated design results do not establish the power or reliability of a 32-task validation gate in our planned setting.

sources.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
sources.verified_material: Metadata, author full text, and official repository.
sources.original_contribution: An archive-based system whose coding agents modify their own implementation and use empirical coding-task outcomes to evaluate revisions.
sources.our_difference: RSI-Audit adopts bounded persistent agent revisions as a controlled testbed and evaluates validation reuse versus fresh validation under matched execution caps. It does not claim DGM-scale performance or unbounded recursive improvement.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Agent self-modification and downstream coding scores alone do not imply a theoretical guarantee of improvement. The paper's historical cost estimate is not a current cloud-price quote.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report
sources.verified_material: Complete author list, submission history, and abstract on arXiv.
sources.original_contribution: Describes the Qwen2.5-Coder family, including a 7B model, its code-oriented pretraining and post-training, and coding evaluations.
sources.our_difference: Used as a frozen reproducible backbone, not a contribution or evidence that the proposed evaluation policy works. Pin the exact model ID, revision, tokenizer, decoding configuration, and serving software before the main experiment.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: The report does not establish that old public EvalPlus tasks are absent from the model's training data. Never call this planned audit contamination-free.

sources.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
sources.verified_material: Metadata, abstract, official repository, and official EvalPlus Hugging Face organization/dataset metadata. The organization lists 164 HumanEval+ and 378 MBPP+ tasks, totaling 542 before any additional filtering.
sources.original_contribution: Expands code benchmarks with LLM-generated and mutation-based test inputs, revealing failures that weaker original tests miss and demonstrating that inadequate tests can change model rankings.
sources.our_difference: Uses strengthened executable tests and disjoint task partitions for longitudinal agent-revision audits. Does not claim to invent mutation testing or enhanced code tests.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Passing finite tests is an operational correctness measure, not a proof. Pin exact dataset revisions, verify the 542-task union locally, and stratify by HumanEval+ versus MBPP+. The 2023 paper alone does not establish the current MBPP+ release size. Semantic deduplication or invalid-task exclusions may reduce the available counts and must be disclosed rather than silently replenished.

sources.title: The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis
sources.verified_material: Primary institutional publication page confirms title, authors, date, publication and contribution; PubMed corroborates journal volume, issue, pages and DOI. Publisher full text returned HTTP 403.
sources.original_contribution: Addresses adaptively selected analyses using ideas from privacy-preserving analysis and constructs a method for safely reusing holdout data under its stated conditions.
sources.our_difference: Provides foundational motivation for measuring adaptive validation effects in agent evolution. RSI-Audit's fixed threshold or fresh-shard comparisons do not implement this method and inherit no differential-privacy or statistical-validity guarantee.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Do not identify a simple repeatedly queried test panel with the paper's Reusable Holdout algorithm. They are different procedures.

sources.title: The Ladder: A Reliable Leaderboard for Machine Learning Competitions
sources.verified_material: Official PMLR publication metadata and abstract.
sources.original_contribution: Formalizes leaderboard accuracy for sequential adaptive submissions and develops a leaderboard algorithm with theoretical guarantees under the paper's model.
sources.our_difference: Motivates treating feedback and repeated validation as experimental variables. RSI-Audit studies fixed small-model agent loops, without claiming to reproduce Ladder or extend its theorem.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Restricting feedback to a scalar or pass/fail does not automatically confer the Ladder guarantee.

sources.title: Certified Long-Horizon Code Agent Evolution via Validation-Gated Skill Optimization
sources.verified_material: Metadata and full text, especially sections 3.3 and B.6-B.7.
sources.original_contribution: Studies validation-gated persistent skill-bank evolution and gives bounds for adaptive validation-panel reuse and holdout sizing. Main experiments reuse 50 validation tasks, with an empirical 0.02 acceptance margin, and evaluate on disjoint tasks.
sources.our_difference: Tests practical validation-allocation policies on a frozen 7B open model with a short fixed horizon and explicit equal execution caps. The focus is small-budget independent auditing and resource tradeoffs, not a new validation gate or new certification theorem.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: It is false to claim prior work ignores adaptive panel reuse. A 32-task gate and six rounds do not replicate VALVE or establish its theoretical assumptions. Report the method as VALVE-inspired only if its implementation is materially simplified.

sources.title: Who Verifies the Verifier? Co-Evolving Inspectable Graders with Self-Improving Agents
sources.verified_material: Primary author-institution publication metadata and full PDF; arXiv ID corroborated by search.
sources.original_contribution: Evolves inspectable compositions of verifier detectors with anchor guards and studies their combination with a skill-evolution loop. An ablation shows that task-score gains alone cannot certify verifier validity.
sources.our_difference: RSI-Audit freezes the executable correctness oracle and varies access to validation tasks. It measures data-reuse and budget-allocation policies rather than co-evolving a grader.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Do not claim to be the first to independently audit self-evolved verification or to identify degeneracy of an evaluator. The existing paper's MBPP+ effects are directionally consistent but its task-clustered tests are not conventionally significant.

sources.title: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards
sources.verified_material: Complete latest author list, abstract and paper structure.
sources.original_contribution: Characterizes coding-agent verification through scalability, faithfulness and robustness, and studies different reward constructions and their failure modes.
sources.our_difference: Provides general motivation; the planned contribution is a narrow reproducible experiment on fixed executable verifiers and validation access under resource caps.
sources.limitations_for_our_claims: Its broad analysis does not establish that fresh validation will beat reuse in this proposed experiment.
